title: The Night Before War
subtitle: The fires of war burn ever nearer. Children of the Don, it's time to unite!

items.text: The Night Before War
Sonetto steps outside, looking out over the endless grassland and to the sky beyond. The afternoon wind rushes from across the steppe, carrying an unseasonable dryness.

It gently rustles through her hair. The weariness from her relentless schedule, the weight of the coming war, and the tension she bears from her responsibilities are, for a brief moment, faintly eased.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Greetings, Ms. Sonetto.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Mr. Igor.
Their greeting is awkward, yet it doesn't stop the tough old admiral from leaning against a tree not far away. He gently closes his eyes, as if listening for something.
How long has he been standing there? Sonetto swallows the question before it reaches her lips.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What are you doing out here?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: There's a sound as the wind brushes over the grasslands. I find it eases my mind.
Sonetto focuses in on the same sound. After a moment, she resumes her questions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You're here for the Timekeeper, is that right?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Is she still resting? What she saw in the Amber Room must have impacted her greatly.
Aware of the old man's special status, Sonetto tightens her grip on the wand hidden behind her back.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I only want to have a word with her. Nothing more.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We're on the same side.
Footsteps crunch through the dirt behind them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: For the time being, yes, until Krutov is defeated.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I owe you an apology, leaving you in the Amber Room for so long. My troops needed their leader when Krutov attacked.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Think nothing of it. I was prepared for the risks. Besides, Sonetto and Marsha were there to help me.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: What did you see there, in the Room?
An overt question.
A fear older than memory floods her vision. After a few deep breaths, reason slowly returns.
Urd

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: I believe it was Urd. She seemed unsure of that herself. There were others there trying to convince her of her own identity.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: She was being put through some kind of disturbing experiment, and for a brief moment, she caught sight of me. She walked towards me, then vanished.

items.text: An experiment

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: I felt like I'd been put into some kind of experiment. But it wasn't me. It was Urd.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: They ran the experiment over and over, each time Urd suffering immense pain. It all seemed designed to transform her into someone else.

items.text: A white room

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: I saw a pure white room, a kind of white I've never seen before. And Urd ... She was sat in a chair at the center of it.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: She was struggling, as if she were in pain. I wanted to help, but I couldn't reach her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I saw other things, too, but they were blurry and fragmented.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The video clips? Then they didn't take their devices with them when they evacuated after all.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, whatever I saw wasn't footage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have to enter the Amber Room once more to make sense of what I saw.
Igor falls silent for a moment, then shakes his head.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I advise against it. There are still skirmishes being fought in the city. No one can guarantee the church will stay safe for long.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The Cavalry Corps is preparing for a surprise assault tonight. Lieutenant Lilya is in the field trying to locate and destroy the Manus's rites. Your assistant will be your only protection.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You're too important, Timekeeper. If your presence in Bereggrad were exposed, the Manus will throw everything they have into capturing you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I cannot afford to let anything jeopardize our battle plan. You must stay hidden from the enemy until it is safe.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ms. Sonetto, I don't question your capability and devotion, but Bereggrad is a potential battlefield. It's too dangerous.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good point. I'll be sure to return to the Amber Room only after you've defeated Krutov.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It will be done soon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A soldier came to me earlier today. He seemed to think a Foundation member would have a higher chance of surviving the battle and asked me to deliver a letter to his brother on the Western Front.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What about you, Mr. Igor? Did you write anything?
Igor lets out a sigh so faint it almost goes unnoticed. Clearly he is trying to conceal something.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I know someone who would be deeply upset were you to die here. She intends to end your life with her own hands.
Igor rubs his temples and gives a helpless smile.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Lopera. Does the Foundation still keep her?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You could say that. She isn't allowed to return to her position as a soldier yet, not until Zeno's review is finished.
Igor nods, signaling he wants to hear more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She's made somewhat of a life for herself at the Foundation. Made friends and got into some trouble.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They've assigned her an instructor to work on her dice game obsession.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Pera, so typical of her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's something I'd like to know, too.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ask away.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Commander Ivan invited me to his home in Tamarovka for a lunch. A lady hosted us.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He introduced her as his "mother," but something seemed off.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: She is indeed Ivan's mother.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then, did Commander Ivan request shelter for her from the "Storm"?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Yes, a request made not long after their reunion.
Igor folds his arms across his chest, frowning.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Not even the most capable diviners could have predicted the advent of the "Storm." As you suspected, Ivan's mother, like most at that time, was reversed during the first "Storm."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Some time after that, Ivan rediscovered her. He told me that he knew it was her from the wrinkles on her face and her tender smile.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He was certain that, by some miracle, his mother had survived the "Storm" and returned to him.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: An improbable scenario, don't you think, Timekeeper?
A familiar coincidence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: One day, I'll uncover the truth about the "Storm," for everyone's sake, for my mother.
Igor doesn't answer. Instead, he fixes his gaze on the rolling waves of grass.
Night falls over the steppe.
Amid the chaos of pounding hooves and shouting voices, Sternova lifts the tent flap.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Colonel Sternova, is the Corps prepared to ride out soon?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Yes. Our forces are assembled. We're ready to go.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: As for the Gryphons, three of their air defense squads have been stationed in Bereggrad, while the rest are heading to Vysokogorye, the mountain north of the city.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is Igor marching with his army?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: No, both Igor and Commander Ivan will stay at the command post in the sich.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: I'm here to check on you at Lieutenant Lilya's request. She said you're good at slipping away and making people worry.
Sonetto suppresses a laugh before deftly steering the conversation elsewhere.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Three squads. That's all the city has for air defense?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: That and the militia. With our reduced numbers and the danger of street battles, we have to rely on the support of armed citizens.
Outside the tent, the agitation has only continued to build. The commander's orders ring out, half-lost in the swelling noise.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Timekeeper, for your own sake, I suggest you leave the Don. Or at least make sure you bunker down someplace safe.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: I'll take my leave of you now. Commander Ivan is about to rally the troops.
Beneath the night's sky, a hushed yet fervent atmosphere settles in. The soldiers' fighting spirits render them restless.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: To think I get to fight a real war! God! My hands won't stop shaking!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Keep your head on straight, you idiot, or you'll get yourself killed. There's nothing romantic about war!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: I've fought alongside many soldiers like you. Dreaming of glory, victory, and the praise of our people when we returned home.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: But I returned alone. The rest died on some godforsaken battlefield, along with their dreams of glory. I visited their graves before I left. Hope their spirits are with me.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: I-I went home too, to see my girl.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: You didn't promise you were going to marry her after we win the war, did you?

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: No, I ... I didn't say anything at all. I just looked into those beautiful eyes of hers. She understood the rest.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: We knew it could be the last time we'd see each other.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Alright, that's enough, lover boy. Commander Ivan's about to give his speech.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Attention all troops! Call the roll!
Strong, unified voices rise from the formations, joined by the thunder of horses stamping the ground.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: All soldiers have returned to their posts, sir. I knew there were no cowards in the Corps.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I expected nothing less.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Listen, riders! You've seen the ruin Krutov and his bandits have wrought.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You've seen those black-hearted cowards burn Cossack homes and kill our kin.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: I'm going to cut off that clown's head and hang it in my backyard!
The young voice sparks a burst of laughter. Then fists and shouts of approval are thrown into the air.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You've seen them rob and trample our land, our people, and our dignity!

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You've heard them laugh as they slaughtered our people and our children wept!

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: But today their villainy ends. Why, my brothers and sisters?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Because we—the Cavalry Corps, riders of the steppe, children of the Don—will stop them in their tracks!

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We will grind them to dust and ride home victorious! For the steppe! For the Don! For Cossack children yet unborn!

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Today, we destroy the enemy and reclaim our home! Forward!

items.speaker: Soldiers
items.text: Ura!
This land, the great mother of the Cossacks, trembles beneath the vigor of her sons and daughters.
At the commander's order, the cavalry formations make their march, the scouts at the front lifting their torches high.
The flames of glory burn bright, setting the curtain of history ablaze.
